docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Cylon is a domain-specific language for defining automated workflows with:

  • Task execution
  • Scheduling
  • Dependencies
  • Conditional logic

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
TASK backupDB {
    RUN "backup.sh"
    EVERY DAY AT 02:00
}

TASK sendReport {
    RUN "report.py"
    AFTER backupDB
    IF SUCCESS
}

TASK cleanup {
    RUN "cleanup.sh"
    EVERY WEEK ON SUNDAY AT 03:00
}

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• backupDB runs daily at 02:00

  • sendReport runs after backupDB if it succeeds

  • cleanup runs weekly on Sunday

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• RUN: RUN "script.sh"

  • MOVE: MOVE "source" TO "destination"

  • SEND: SEND "message" TO "user"

  • GENERATE: GENERATE "file.pdf"

  • EXPORT: EXPORT "data.csv"

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text:
• Daily: EVERY DAY AT 02:00

  • Weekly: EVERY WEEK ON SUNDAY AT 03:00

docs.title: Dependencies & Conditions
docs.text:
• Dependencies: AFTER taskName or BEFORE taskName

  • Conditions: IF SUCCESS or IF FAILED

docs.title: Execution Model
docs.text:
1. Parse all tasks

  2. Store task definitions

  3. Validate:

  4. Duplicate task names

  5. Undefined dependencies

  6. Circular dependencies

  7. Execute tasks

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
• Duplicate Task: Duplicate task name

  • Undefined Dependency: Task depends on undefined task

-Circular Dependency: Circular dependency detected

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No parallel execution

  • No retries

  • Basic condition support only
